title: Strang's and Baron's chief reason: otherwise our sins would be imputed to God
source_text: XXXVIII. Ut autem sic sentiat, eo praecipue se moveri testatur, quod si ad omnes peccati actiones Deus necessario diabolos hominesque impios determinaret, inde sequi existimat peccata nostra Deo merito imputari posse: qua etiam ratione se maxime permotum affirmat Robertus Baronius ille supra citatus.
pass_a_gloss: But that he thinks so, he testifies he is moved chiefly by this, that if God necessarily determined devils and impious men to all the actions of sin, thence he thinks it follows that our sins could deservedly be imputed to God: by which reason also that Robert Baron cited above affirms that he was most moved.
pass_b_english: Strang says he holds this view chiefly because, if God necessarily determined devils and wicked men to every action of sin, it would follow, in his judgment, that our sins could rightly be charged to God.
Robert Baron, cited above, says this was the reason that weighed most with him as well.

lemmas.gloss: could deservedly be imputed to God

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
